title: Quarter Tilt: Operational Slate & Decision Tracker (Q3→Q4 bridge) v0.1
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working planning doc intended to: align leadership on the minimal set of priorities to carry from Q3 into Q4 (the "tilt"), capture contingencies across three staffing/capacity scenarios, and produce a concise all‑hands agenda and exec update we can ship next week. Treat this as: opinionated + operational.

Top-level ask
---
Decide by 2025-07-22: Which of the three tilt packages (Conserve / Balance / Accelerate) becomes our default runbook for the next 90 days. That decision determines hiring focus, Dedicated capacity commitments, and the all‑hands narrative.

Bellwether metrics (what we will watch for decisioning)
- Platform latency p50/p95 (hosted API) — targets: p50 < 90ms, p95 < 450ms
- Token cost/unit trend (rolling 14d) — flag if > 12% week-over-week increase
- Dedicated utilization (percent of reserved GPU capacity used for production) — threshold: > 78% triggers immediate capacity plan
- Customer SLA incidents (sev>=2) — >2 in 14 days => escalate to SRE-on-call + exec notify

Tilt packages (summary)
1) Conserve (low risk / budget-first) — move non-critical experiments to queued backlog, strict batching and cache defaults, freeze Dedicated expansion. Focus: reliability, cost controls, documentation updates.
2) Balance (default recommendation) — pursue two strategic bets (Optimize batching & private deployments sales), limited Dedicated bursts, hire 2 infra/serving engineers.
3) Accelerate (growth-first) — commit to Dedicated expansion, prioritize new features (streaming improvements, function-calling SDK), hire 6 engineers, run two paid GTM pilots.

Draft OKRs (Q3 end → Q4 start window) — v0.1
- Objective A: Keep production quality and cost stable through the tilt
  - KR1: p95 latency within 1.2x baseline across 95% of routes
  - KR2: Token cost per 1k tokens down 6% vs. previous quarter (measured by Optimize suggestions enacted)
  - KR3: < 2 Sev>=2 incidents per 30 days
- Objective B: Make Dedicated capacity adoption frictionless for 3 anchor customers
  - KR1: Launch dedicated onboarding playbook and reduce time-to-first-request to < 48 hours for pilot customers
  - KR2: Signed pilot agreements with 2 customers and one internal production migration
- Objective C (if Accelerate chosen): Reduce end-to-end streaming latency by 30% for large-response flows
  - KR1: End-to-end median stream lag reduced by 30% on test harness

Staffing & capacity scenarios (high level)
- Scenario Conserve: hiring freeze for non-critical roles; repurpose contractor budget; postpone two performance hires. Impact: slower feature velocity, lower spend.
- Scenario Balance: hire 2 infra/serving; maintain contractor slots; fund 1 GTM pilot.
- Scenario Accelerate: hire 6 (4 infra/serving, 2 SDK/console), reserve +20% Dedicated burst capacity (Q4 commit).

All‑Hands: proposed run-of-show (45 minutes)
- Opening (5m) — CEO quick framing: "Tilt" decision and why it matters
- Platform pulse (8m) — SRE/serving leads: metrics snapshot and bellwether explanation (show p50/p95, token cost trends)
- Product priorities (7m) — two slides: what we will pause vs. accelerate under chosen tilt
- Customer & GTM (7m) — sales highlight of pilot opportunities and expected ramp
- Team asks (10m) — explicit asks by function (see below) + where to triage ideas
- Q&A (8m) — pre-submitted questions prioritized, live slack channel for follow-ups

Team asks (short)
- Eng (serving/runtime): codify short-term batching defaults; doc changes in /docs/tilt; owner: Devon Patel; due: 2025-07-24
- Product: freeze non-essential feature RFCs and publish a sprint commitment list; owner: Asha Raman; due: 2025-07-23
- SRE/Infra: run capacity stress pass for Dedicated + burst scenario and provide cost delta; owner: Mariana Ortega; due: 2025-07-25
- GTM: prepare 2 pilot briefs and one customer-facing one-pager; owner: Sofia Martins; due: 2025-07-28

Decision tracker (working log)
- 2025-07-12: Draft tilt packages created (Liam) — open
- 2025-07-14: Bellwether metric set agreed in leadership sync — open
- 2025-07-18: Proposed All‑Hands run-of-show posted for review — feedback due 2025-07-20
- Decision due: 2025-07-22 — which tilt package to adopt (owner: CEO + execs)

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Choosing Accelerate without firm pilot commitments => cost overrun. Mitigation: require 2 signed paid pilots before Q4 Dedicated commit.
- Risk: Conserve causes customer churn on performance-sensitive routes. Mitigation: carve out performance-critical routes for exempt status and continue optimization work there.
- Risk: Conflicting org priorities create council drift. Mitigation: weekly 15m tilt standup with exec leads until decision made.

Comms plan (internal + external)
- Internal: All‑hands + short post with decision and what it means for each function (template ready).
- External: Support-run emails to pilot customers if we elect Accelerate; otherwise delayed for Balance/Conserve.

Open questions (leadership input required)
1) If we choose Balance, which single dedicated feature do we prioritize to show forward momentum? (ops: recommended – Dedicated onboarding playbook)
2) What is the absolute budget ceiling for Q4 Dedicated commitment if we go Accelerate? Need finance sign-off.
3) Are there legal/compliance blockers for faster Private deployments for pilot customers? (Legal input asked)

Immediate next steps (owner: Liam Chen)
- Collate feedback on this doc by 2025-07-20 EOD (comment threads only)
- Lock Bellwether dashboards and share links for exec review (Mariana) — target 2025-07-21
- Finalize All‑Hands slide deck and rehearsal slot (Asha + DevEx) — target 2025-07-21

Notes to reviewers
- This is purposely compact. The goal is to have an adoptable operational posture (the "tilt") with explicit, measurable signals. Please surface major objections in comments — particularly on the Bellwether metric thresholds and staffing assumptions.
